question: Should malformed pullAudio chunks count toward the existing five-consecutive-input-error cutoff and close the Google Meet audio bridge, or should they be discarded without advancing the shutdown counter?
rationale: Both choices are technically viable, but they trade bounded recovery from a corrupt node against continuity of an active meeting and therefore require explicit product/runtime ownership rather than automated judgment.

options.title: Use the existing cutoff
options.body: Treat each malformed chunk as an input failure and stop after five consecutive failures, matching other repeated node-input failures and preventing indefinite corrupt-input churn.

options.title: Discard and continue
options.body: Reject malformed chunks before providers but leave the bridge running, avoiding call interruption at the cost of potentially unbounded warnings from a persistently corrupt node.

recommendation.title: Use the existing cutoff
recommendation.body: Treat each malformed chunk as an input failure and stop after five consecutive failures, matching other repeated node-input failures and preventing indefinite corrupt-input churn.
